name: capp_multicell_1710
title: CAPP multiple-cell ("pizza") cavity concept: ideal sector cells and multi-cell vs multi-cavity

citations.authors_short: J. Jeong, S. Youn, S. Ahn, J. E. Kim, Y. K. Semertzidis

software.solver_type: eigenmode (Numerical) and driven with axion source (Numerical^ax)
software.boundary: Table 2: copper impedance walls, no end caps

geometry.description: Table 2/3: ideal circular-sector cells, radius Rc = 25 mm, N = 2,4,6,8 cells of angle theta = 2 pi/N, zero-thickness PEC-like partitions meeting on the axis, infinite length ("no end caps"). Table 1: 100 mm magnet bore, cavity height 200 mm, wall thickness 5 mm, quad-cavity (4 separate cylinders) vs quad-cell vs sext-cell. Prototype (Sec. 5): double-cell OFHC, 90 mm ID, 100 mm length, 5 mm wall, 10 mm hollow gap, alumina rods

inner_radius_table1.note: quad-cavity: 4 cylinders of R ~15.7 mm (from f = 7.30 GHz and V = 0.62 L)

partition_thickness_table1.note: V = 1.08 L (quad) and 1.02 L (sext) vs pi*45^2*200 = 1.272 L imply ~5 mm partitions

center_gap_table1.note: Sec. 3.4 optimum for quad-cell is d/D = 0.1

tuning_rod.value: eps_r = 10 lossless, r/R = 0.1 (simulation); 99.5% Al2O3 in the prototype

conventions.form_factor_definition: C = |int E.B0 dV|^2 / (int eps|E|^2 dV int |B0|^2 dV) (Eq. 2)
conventions.Q_definition: Q = omega U / P_loss with P_loss = (1/(2 sigma mu^2 delta)) int |n x B|^2 dA (Eqs. 12-14); Table 2 excludes end caps
conventions.notes: Table 3 ratios are relative to the empty cylinder (N=0) of the same Rc at its own frequency

tables.description: multi-cavity vs multi-cell in a 100 mm bore (COMSOL, RT, unloaded Q); P and df/dt relative to quad-cavity
Q of N-cell cavity, no end caps, Rc = 25 mm, sigma = 5.96e7 S/m; parentheses = % deviation from analytic
TM010-like frequency, Q and loss ratio relative to N = 0 (same geometry as Table 2)

analytic_check.description: closed-form TM_{nu 1} sector mode, Ez = J_nu(chi r/Rc) sin(nu phi), nu = N/2, computed by digitize/capp_sector_analytic.py (quadrature to 1e-13): Q = (2/delta) k^2 int|Ez|^2 dA / oint|dEz/dn|^2 dl, C = |int Ez dA|^2/(A int|Ez|^2 dA)
findings: omega/omega0, Q/Q0, Prad/Pazi (0.849 vs printed 0.84 for N=2; others agree to rounding) and C reproduce Table 3 / 2205.01319 Table 2

our analytic Q with the stated sigma = 5.96e7 S/m is 0.32% BELOW the paper analytic values for every N; the constant ratio implies the paper effectively used sigma = 5.998e+07 S/m, which is exactly COMSOL's built-in copper (5.998e7 S/m) - the likely explanation (analytic column evaluated with the material-library value, not the caption value). Use our closed form (stated sigma) as the axionFEM target; the paper COMSOL values agree with it to +0.46/+0.32/+0.25/-0.12 % (N = 2/4/6/8)
C (uniform Bz) is the same for one cell and for all N cells in phase: 0.6440 / 0.6493 / 0.6341 / 0.6132 for N = 2/4/6/8

measured_values.note: Fig. 9 measured mode map not digitized (rod positions unknown, measurement only)

gaps.parameter: Table 1 partition thickness, centre gap, rod presence
gaps.proposal: infer from volumes (5 mm partitions; V(quad) = 1.08 L suggests partitions nearly to the axis, V(sext) = 1.02 L suggests a ~4.5 mm gap); sweep t in {0, 5 mm} and Rg in {0, 0.05, 0.1}*Rc and match f and V; treat Table 1 as P2 sanity only

gaps.issue: alumina rod diameter and trajectory not given

inconsistencies.description: Table 2 analytic Q vs stated sigma
inconsistencies.evidence: closed form with sigma = 5.96e7 S/m gives 17737.5/16099.9/14274.8/12866.1, uniformly 0.32% below the printed 17794/16151/14320/12907; the implied sigma = 5.998e7 S/m equals COMSOL's built-in copper conductivity (likely explanation: the analytic column used the COMSOL material value)
inconsistencies.proposal: benchmark against the closed form with the stated sigma (or with 5.998e7 to compare digit-for-digit with the paper); quote the paper COMSOL numbers as secondary (agreement within 0.5%)

inconsistencies.description: mode naming of the double-cell prototype
inconsistencies.evidence: Sec. 3.3/5 text: second mode is TM110-like; Fig. 9 caption: "TM011-like"; Fig. 7 caption: "TM010-like and TM020-like"
inconsistencies.proposal: irrelevant for the ideal-sector benchmark; ignore

inconsistencies.evidence: Sec. 5: TM010-like at 4.2 GHz; Fig. 9 tuning range 3.6-4.0 GHz
inconsistencies.proposal: 4.2 GHz presumably without rods (empty double cell: chi11 c/(2 pi 45 mm) = 4.06 GHz for zero-thickness partition, higher with 5 mm partition) - unverified

inconsistencies.description: Eq. 16 (loss ratio P_rad/P_azi) has a typo in the paper itself (rendered p.3, not an extraction artefact)
inconsistencies.evidence: with J_{n/2}(chi) = 0 the printed form reduces to 4 n^3/(pi (n^2 - 1)) = 3.40 at n = 2, vs Table 3 0.84. With the denominator corrected to (J_{n/2-1}(chi) - J_{n/2+1}(chi))^2 it reduces to n^3/(pi (n^2 - 1)) = 0.849/1.358/1.964/2.587 for n = 2/4/6/8 = Table 3 (0.84/1.36/1.96/2.59) and = our quadrature
inconsistencies.proposal: use the corrected closed form n^3/(pi (n^2 - 1)) (n = number of cells) or the direct integral

inconsistencies.evidence: Eq. 2 integrates |B0|^2 over "the cavity volume" without saying whether partitions are excluded. For Tables 2-3 (zero-thickness partitions) the question is moot. Table 1 gives V = 1.08 L (quad-cell) and 1.02 L (sext-cell) vs pi 45^2 200 mm^3 = 1.272 L for the full 90 mm x 200 mm bore cylinder, i.e. V is the vacuum volume (partitions excluded, 15% / 20% of the cylinder); its relative columns follow P ~ C V Q (1.636 vs printed 1.65 quad-cell, 1.326 vs 1.32 sext-cell) and df/dt ~ C^2 V^2 Q (2.68 vs 2.72, 1.99 vs 1.98), so C is quoted together with the vacuum V. Whether C itself was normalized by V_vac is not stated
inconsistencies.proposal: for Table 1, report axionFEM C both ways (V = vacuum volume and V = full cylinder) and compare the products C V

solver_class.reason: ideal sector cells are z-invariant TM modes: a 2D scalar Helmholtz problem on the sector (or a 3D extrusion with PEC/impedance ends). Not axisymmetric. Closed forms exist (P0 analytic check, no FEM needed). Table 1 and the prototype need 3D

priority_reason: closed-form analytic reference for f, Q (walls only), C; tabulated COMSOL agrees to <0.5%

readme_row.quantities: Tab 2: Q (no end caps) for 2/4/6/8 sector cells; Tab 3: w/w0, Q/Q0, loss ratio; Tab 1: f, Q, C, V; closed-form check
